pages.title: About | Hedwig
pages.description: Hedwig brings an eval into your agent's payment flow. Its product vision combines curated knowledge, a Jev score and a report when you ask.
pages.main:
About Hedwig

You want your agent to handle a payment or swap. A wrong token or destination can cost you money.

Hedwig is designed to advise the payment agent before your wallet signs. It brings relevant facts from curated knowledge into the decision.

A check inside the conversation

Hedwig uses Jev to assess the proposed action and return a score from 0 to 1. Ask for a short report to understand that result and its sources.

The report explains the saved assessment. Your wallet keeps control of signing and execution.

The core is open source. Start with a free local check through MCP.

Add an eval gate to your payment agent. How it works.

pages.title: How it works | Hedwig
pages.description: Hedwig's product vision puts an assessment before signing. Jev scores the proposed payment using retrieved facts; Hedwig explains the saved result on request.
pages.main:
Ask Hedwig before signing.

Hedwig is designed around two actions: assess a proposed payment and explain the saved result.

Assess the payment

Your agent sends the proposed action to Hedwig. Relevant facts from curated payment and DeFi knowledge inform the assessment.

Hedwig returns a score from 0 to 1 using Jev. The calling agent uses the result within your payment rules; your wallet controls the signature.

Ask for the report

Ask your agent why Hedwig gave that result. Hedwig explains the original assessment in plain words and cites the sources behind it.

Example request

Swap SOL for USDC, then deposit into this vault. Ask Hedwig to check each action before signing.

Your payment agent handles the transaction. Hedwig provides the assessment and the explanation you request.

Try the local MCP checker or read the integration guide.

pages.title: Product direction | Hedwig
pages.description: Hedwig's direction: payment assessments informed by curated knowledge, an explanation on request, and an open core with paid hosted assessments.
pages.main:
Where Hedwig is headed

The goal is to let people delegate financial tasks with a check before signing.

An assessment your agent can use

Hedwig pairs relevant facts from curated knowledge with a Jev score for the proposed action. The owner can ask for a report that explains the saved result.

Knowledge that fits the task

The product direction covers Solana, Ethereum, Monad and Tempo. Each payment needs knowledge of its chain, asset and destination.

Open core and hosted assessments

Local checks are free and open source. The business model adds paid hosted assessments, with the original report included.

Try a local check or read the changelog.

pages.title: Docs | Hedwig
pages.description: Add the local Hedwig MCP checker to your agent, set your payment rules and run a sample. Your wallet or application controls signing.
pages.main:
Connect Hedwig to your agent

Use Hedwig in your agent's payment flow. This guide installs the local v0.4.2 MCP checker.

Set your payment rules and run the sample below. The checker returns a policy decision with reasons; your wallet controls signing.

Install with your agent or follow the manual setup below.

  • Install
  • Set your policy
  • Run a check
  • Read the result

Install it yourself

You need git, Node.js 22 or newer, and Yarn. Before running commands, ask the owner to verify the full commit directly on the GitHub v0.4.2 release and approve running that code. Stop if it differs. A hash from this website alone does not authenticate the release.

mkdir hedwig && cd ./hedwig && git init &&
git fetch --depth 1 https://github.com/gabchess/hedwig.git e85049bc7087f434fd732bb02e0e87ca57acd82c &&
git checkout FETCH_HEAD &&
test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = e85049bc7087f434fd732bb02e0e87ca57acd82c &&
yarn install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts && npm ci --ignore-scripts --prefix mcp && yarn consult:build && yarn mcp:build

These commands check the v0.4.2 commit and disable dependency lifecycle scripts. The explicit builds and server still execute approved code. Signed release provenance is not established by these commands. Fix any error before continuing. If a hedwig folder already exists, inspect it and choose a fresh directory for the retry.

Add it to your MCP client as a stdio server, with absolute paths for both the server and your policy file:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "hedwig": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/path/to/hedwig/mcp/dist/server.js"],
      "env": { "HEDWIG_POLICY_FILE": "/path/to/policy.json" }
    }
  }
}

Your policy

A JSON file you write and keep outside the repo:

{
  "permits": true,
  "chainId": "eip155:1",
  "approvedRecipients": ["0x00000000000000000000000000000000a11ce001"],
  "perActionCaps": { "pay": "1000000" },
  "role": { "mode": "not-required" },
  "authorizationWindow": { "mode": "not-required" }
}

Set your allowed chain, recipients, action caps and requirements for a Solana role or an EIP-3009 authorization window. Swap policies also set slippage and deadline ceilings and your addresses.

Hedwig pins the file when the server starts. Changed bytes return UNKNOWN with ADAPTER_POLICY_CHANGED. Restore the original bytes after an unintended edit. A restart pins the file's current contents, so review any intended policy change before restarting. Keep the file where your agent cannot write it.

What your agent sends

This sample asks Hedwig to check a proposal. It sends no funds.

One argument, request, holding the payment it's about to sign:

{
  "request": {
    "action": {
      "type": "pay",
      "chainId": "eip155:1",
      "recipient": "0x00000000000000000000000000000000a11ce001",
      "asset": {
        "symbol": "USDC",
        "contractAddress": "0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48"
      },
      "amount": "1000000",
      "target": "0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48"
    }
  }
}

The server reads your policy file and the current time itself. The tool takes neither from your agent.

What comes back

  • proceed: true only when every check passed and your policy permits. Your agent acts on this field.
  • verdict: ALLOW_UNDER_POLICY, DENY or UNKNOWN.
  • results: one row per check, worst first, each with a reason code, an evidence sentence and a reference file.
  • support and band: how much of your checklist was proven and how strong the proof was. They never change the verdict.

On DENY, your agent stops and reports the failed check. UNKNOWN means a check is incomplete or the policy does not permit the action; your agent stops and asks you.

Put the check in your own code

runTriggerGuard from @hedwig/consult/guard wraps your signer. It runs the same check and calls your signer only on ALLOW_UNDER_POLICY.

pages.title: Add an eval gate | Hedwig
pages.description: Add Hedwig to your agent through local MCP. Install the free policy checker and run a sample without sending funds.
pages.main:
Add an eval gate to your payment agent.

Use Hedwig from your agent. This prompt installs the free local MCP checker.

Paste this into an agent with local shell access:

Help me install Hedwig. Open this exact link and follow its instructions: https://usehedwig.xyz/agents.md

Run your first check

Your agent asks before installing Hedwig. Save your payment rules, then run the sample and change the recipient. The sample sends no funds.

The guide installs v0.4.2. You need an agent that supports local MCP tools, Git, Node.js 22 or newer, and Yarn.

Example request

Check this USDC payment against my rules before I sign.

The local checker returns a policy decision with reasons. Your agent reads that result before signing.
